label: copy-phase input s/z/p/b (rare, context-gated)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99% of mass), and almost only on steps where the fed-back input is s (39% of mass), z, p or b (85% together; h and 2 add a little). It does not fire on the original-phase tokens, on <DEL>, or on the first occurrence of a token. It is very sparse, though: only about 0.8% of copy-phase s/z/p/b inputs activate it, so precision is very low. Restricting the output token (h, m, i, s, 1, ...) or the next output (v, h, x, u, ...) raises precision to about 10% at the cost of recall, and I found no simple variable that picks out which instances fire. Firing rate rises with later positions and longer sequences (L = 9 holds 44% of mass), with a bump at recall_idx = 2. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.12, max 0.24), and I found nothing that reliably modulates it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+6.28), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+4.01), phase=2 & out_tok=h (+3.54), in_tok=2 (+3.32), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+3.12), phase=2 & in_tok=b (+2.85).
